statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because no fresh independent NQ source confirms persistent one-way structure, while the U.S. 10-year yield above 5.02%, Brent near $107 and semiconductor weakness keep Stress extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The primary danger window is the 12:30 UTC Empire State release through the first full U.S. cash-session hour; higher Tail states remain conditional on observed directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks or failed retracements.
headline: Low Tail persists as yields above 5% and oil near $107 keep Stress extreme
body: Fresh Reuters reporting shows the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield above 5.02%, Brent above $107 and S&P e-minis modestly lower as Asian equities weaken. No sufficiently current independent source establishes persistent one-way NQ structure, so Tail remains low while cross-asset Stress is extreme.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC clock hours, Tail was elevated through much of Monday's overnight and U.S. session, peaking at 32%, then fell as substantial mean reversion developed. WATCH persisted at 16-17 UTC and briefly at 20 UTC; Tail stayed low from 21 UTC through 05 UTC.
outlookSummary: Current Tail remains low because persistent one-way NQ structure is not independently verified, while oil above $107 and Treasury yields above 5% keep Stress extreme. Conditional Tail rises into the 12:30 UTC Empire State release and 13:30 UTC cash open, peaking at 24% WATCH only if price discovery becomes persistently directional with shallow or failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: Reuters reports the U.S. 10-year yield above 5.02%, Brent near $107.37 and S&P e-minis down 0.22%. No fresh independent NQ path source confirms persistent mean-reversion failure, so Tail remains low while Stress is extreme.
drivers: No fresh independent NQ mean-reversion-failure evidence

forecast.analysis: At the European open, elevated oil and yields can amplify pressure, but Tail stays low unless NQ confirms directional efficiency through repeated extension or failed retracements.
drivers: European open; repeated extension or failed retracements are the Tail trigger

forecast.analysis: Early Europe tests whether overnight macro stress becomes a one-way equity path. Rotational or retracing trade would keep Tail below WATCH.
Mid-European trade remains a transition hour. Tail would rise only if NQ starts carrying a persistent directional structure into the U.S. premarket.
drivers: Europe-to-U.S. transition; persistent directional NQ structure required

forecast.analysis: The final pre-event hour keeps high Stress from oil, rates and chip weakness. Tail remains low unless NQ begins holding near extremes with weak retracement capacity.
drivers: Pre-event positioning ahead of Empire State
Extreme-holding and shallow pullbacks are the escalation signals

forecast.analysis: Empire State Manufacturing is scheduled for 12:30 UTC. WATCH is conditional on the release producing persistent directional price discovery rather than on the event itself.
The 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open is the highest-risk checkpoint. WATCH reflects conditional opening-auction continuation, shallow pullbacks or repeated failed retracements.
drivers: Opening-auction continuation and failed pullbacks are the key Tail tests

forecast.analysis: The first full cash-session hour remains WATCH only if the opening move keeps extending and meaningful retracement does not develop; orderly two-way discovery would lower Tail quickly.
drivers: Meaningful retracement would quickly reduce Tail

forecast.analysis: After the initial opening sequence, the baseline returns to low Tail if price discovery broadens and retracements reappear. Stress can remain extreme without a pathological path.
drivers: High Stress may persist without a one-way path

forecast.analysis: Late U.S. morning remains sensitive to yields, oil and semiconductor weakness. Tail stays low unless an earlier directional move resumes after failed pullbacks.
drivers: Renewed extension after failed pullbacks would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: Near the U.S. midday transition, fading directional efficiency would support low Tail; renewed extension from session extremes would be the key contrary signal.
drivers: Directional efficiency versus retracement is the key distinction

forecast.analysis: Midday liquidity can exaggerate moves, but Tail remains low absent repeated extension and failed retracement. Cross-asset stress is expected to remain elevated.
drivers: Repeated extension is required for higher Tail

forecast.analysis: Early afternoon risk moderates if the session continues to retrace. A renewed one-way move aligned with yields, oil and semiconductors would be the escalation path.
drivers: Oil, yields and semiconductors remain conditional amplifiers

forecast.analysis: Into the U.S. power-hour approach, Tail stays low unless NQ holds near an extreme and pullbacks repeatedly fail while cross-asset pressure remains aligned.
drivers: Session-extreme holding would be the main escalation signal

forecast.analysis: During power hour, a persistent trend can re-emerge, but WATCH is not assumed. Low Tail requires continued evidence of two-way price discovery or meaningful retracement.
drivers: Persistent trend continuation is the conditional Tail risk

forecast.analysis: After the cash close, headline and gap risk remain elevated, while Tail stays low unless post-close futures establish sustained directional continuation.
drivers: Headline and gap risk remain elevated

forecast.analysis: Early U.S. evening remains dominated by oil, rates and Fed-event uncertainty. Without fresh one-way futures structure, the conditional Tail baseline remains low.
drivers: No one-way futures structure is assumed

forecast.analysis: Late U.S. evening is expected to remain high-Stress but low-Tail if futures trade rotationally; geopolitical escalation would be a conditional amplifier.
drivers: Rotational futures trade would keep Tail low

forecast.analysis: At the next Asian open, new regional risk transmission matters only if NQ futures confirm it with sustained extension and limited retracement.
Early Asia remains a low-Tail baseline under two-sided trade. A renewed semiconductor-led global selloff would need NQ price-path confirmation to lift Tail.
drivers: Persistent NQ extension is the required Tail evidence

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asia risk stays conditional on whether oil and global yields keep rising. Stress can remain high while Tail stays low if NQ continues to retrace.
drivers: Stress can stay high even with low Tail

forecast.analysis: Late Asia begins to look toward Wednesday's U.S. Retail Sales and FOMC decision. Event proximity raises Stress, not Tail, before observed directional structure appears.
drivers: Wednesday Retail Sales and FOMC later in the day
Event proximity raises Stress before price-path confirmation

forecast.analysis: The Asia-Europe handoff keeps Tail low by default. Risk would rise only if overnight price action becomes persistently one-way ahead of the later U.S. data cycle.
drivers: Overnight one-way structure would be the escalation condition
